atoms.b: Congress is a bicameral system and therefore has two ((++chambers rooms villages)): The House of Representatives and the ((++Senate Oval_Office White_House)) who both have to pass a bill before it can become a law. Each house has the power to propose a ((++bill paper right)) but can also veto a bill suggested by the other.

hint.text:
bicameral – zweikammerig
Eine Regierung, in der die gesetzgebende Institution in zwei Gruppen unterteilt ist. Dem zugrunde liegt das Prinzip der Gewaltenteilung.

atoms.b: Congress works as the U.S. ((++legislative executive judicial)) branch which writes, debates, and passes laws, controls spending, declares war, and ((++oversees ignores supports)) the executive branch.

However, even though only Congress can declare war, the President as Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces can launch a nuclear missile or send ((++troops votes help)) anywhere in accordance with the law. This raises questions about the success of the ((++separation collapse unity)) of powers.

atoms.text: The House of Representatives — often simply called the House — is comparable to Germany’s Bundestag. Bills that propose to raise revenue must originate in the House of Representatives. Its members are elected to two-year terms and represent the residents of individual congressional districts. The House has a fixed total of 435 members, with seats distributed among the 50 U.S. states according to their population. Although an impeachment trial takes place at the Senate, the House has the sole power of impeachment.

atoms.text: The Senate is comparable to the Bundesrat. It has the unique power to confirm presidential nominations and approve treaties. The Senate consists of two representatives from each state, for a total of 100 senators. Senators serve six-year terms, with one-third of the chamber being renewed every two years. The Senate is where impeachment trials take place.
